headline: Managing Director & Partner at BCG | Leader Greentech, Machinery & Industrial Tech in Europe, Middle East, South America & Africa
about:
I am a Managing Director and Partner at Boston Consulting Group, based in Hamburg. At BCG, I lead our “Greentech, Machinery & Industrial Tech” sector across Europe, the Middle East, South America, and Africa (EMESA).

Since joining BCG in 2007, I’ve lived and worked in our offices in India (New Delhi) and the United States (Chicago), and have spent significant time in China.

I work passionately with corporations and SMEs on performance, technology, and organizational transformations — always with a sharp focus on empowering leaders to unlock sizable and sustainable value.

My background is in mechanical engineering (RWTH Aachen, Germany), where I completed my diploma thesis in Suzhou, China. I also hold a PhD from Ulm University, Germany.

Outside of work, I recharge by spending time with my wonderful wife and two daughters, running, and cooking (mostly) healthy meals with family, friends, and colleagues.

publications.publishedAt: Asia Pacific Medical Technology Association (APACMed) · Nov 1, 2021
publications.description: This white paper explores the ongoing digital transformation of China’s medical device and technologies industry, highlighting how increasing digitalization across healthcare delivery, regulatory processes, and market access models is reshaping the competitive landscape. The report examines key trends driving innovation — such as interoperability of medical technologies, integration of digital data across care pathways, and the growing emphasis on real-world evidence — as well as the regulatory, infrastructure, and adoption challenges that medtech companies face in China’s evolving healthcare ecosystem. It highlights legal risks, procedural requirements for genetic data and samples, and recommendations for proactive enterprise-level management in the context of intensifying legal and regulatory scrutiny.

about:
20 years of leadership in investment and strategy consulting spanning multiple regions and sectors in Industrial Goods.  Deep expertise in business and corporate strategy and significant experience in operations, marketing and sales and M&A transactions.

Simon Rees leads Boston Consulting Group’s Corporate Finance & Strategy practice in the Great Lakes region of North America. Simon works with both public and private sector clients on a wide range of business and enterprise level strategic issues. He is a member of the Industrial Goods practice leadership team where he is the lead for greentech, machinery, and automation in North America. In addition, he helps drive the firm’s work in industrial services, and has a leadership role within BCG’s Center for Climate Action.

Simon works with clients from all types of industrial goods companies, including the adjacent medical devices space and the public sector. He has particularly deep expertise with machinery clients, including those in the automotive, off-highway, aerospace, industrial automation, and building technology industries, as well as general machinery and components. He is also experienced in building materials, chemicals, and industrial distribution.

Simon’s work covers, among other things, business, corporate, and public enterprise strategy, transactions, large-scale transformations, marketing/sales/pricing, and operations. He has particularly deep expertise in industrial services and digital transformation.

Simon sits on the leadership team for BCG's Pride Network. Prior to joining BCG, he worked in investment banking, managing M&A activities for a set of infrastructure funds at Macquarie Bank in London.

about:
I am a Managing Director & Partner in the Minneapolis office of The Boston Consulting Group, which I joined in 2010.  I have developed deep expertise in strategy, marketing, corporate development, and large scale transformations with global medtech and biopharma companies.  I serve as a core member of BCG’s Healthcare Practice Area, and specifically as a lead in our North America MedTech practice and the Healthcare node for the Minneapolis office.  Functionally, I am a core member of BCG's Marketing, Strategy, and Corporate Development practices and am a lead in the topic of Marketing in MedTech. 

My work has spanned the globe and involved a wide range of studies, including growth strategy, marketing transformation, corporate transformation, governance, organizational re-design, post-merger integration, and many other topics.  I spent a year in BCG's Dubai office as part of our Ambassador Program, a program designed to promote an enhanced understanding of business in international contexts.  While I support multinationals and companies based across the globe, I have a keen interest in serving companies the support the healthcare ecosystem in the Twin Cities.

I hold an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, a Masters in Computer Science from Johns Hopkins University, and a Bachelors in Computer Science & Engineering from the University of Michigan.  I spend my spare time with family & friends, enjoy both college and professional football, and serve as Board chair of the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS).

I lead BCG's Chemical Practice in Asia, and have considerable experience and expertise in this sector.

I have a good balance of strategy and problem solving experience from Consulting and ‘hands-on’ sales and operational experience from the Industry. In Consulting, I have helped solve some of the biggest problems across industries (e.g. preparing the World’s largest IPO, launching a payments platform to disrupt fuel retail markets, supporting the carve-out of a large vertically integrated company, mergers of global corporations). For one of the ventures (focused on Payments), I was directly involved in developing the product, the go-to-market strategy and the venture build -  hired a team of 30+ people to rapidly scale the venture to 700+ retail stations and > 500,000 users in less than a year.

I have excellent interpersonal and communication skills with strong executive presence (worked with multiple CEOs & EVPs of multi-billion dollar companies globally). I have managed direct reports as well as indirect reports throughout my career, as well as mentored many through formal and informal networks.

headline: Senior Advisor and Leadership Coach at BCG; Co-Author, Trillions; Visiting Scholar at Tufts University; Research Fellow Emeritus, Autodesk; Founding Advisor for collective intelligence and design science, CELL.
about:
Mickey McManus is a pioneer in the field of strategy, innovation, pervasive computing, human-centered design and education. He holds 12 patents in the areas of connected products, vehicles, and services. He is a leadership coach to high-potential executives, a senior advisor at BCG, and research fellow emeritus at Autodesk.

At Autodesk he was a key member of their corporate strategy, future of learning, and strategic foresights teams and helped pioneer and build their team of c-level visiting fellows. While exploring creative authoring tools he helped them explore how teams would use creative AI, embedded sensing and generative design tools to explore a vastly larger landscape of potential solutions, and close the loop between designing, making, using and evolving the things and places that make up our physical world. He co-created their learning engine initiative where machine learners help human learners thrive over their lifetimes.

He was the CEO and later chairman of MAYA (now a foundational part of BCG.X), one of MAYA's startups is now a part of Nielsen, another is a part of General Dynamics Mission Systems, another formed the basis of Idealab NYC, and the educational institute, LUMA Institute (now the underlying co-creation operating system for Mural) has taught over 70,000 people globally how to co-create with people and make the right thing, right.

Mickey co-authored Trillions: Thriving in the Emerging Information Ecology (Wiley 2012). The book is a field guide to the future, where computing will cease to be confined to any particular "box," but instead be freely accessible in the ambient environment. John C. Abell, former New York Bureau Chief of Wired and founding editor of Reuter.com noted that, “With Trillions authors Lucas, Ballay and McManus belly up to the bar alongside futurists Alvin Toffler, Kevin Kelly and Arthur C. Clark, offering a vision so compellingly argued you’ll only be surprised if it doesn’t happen.”

Trillions was awarded the Axiom Gold Award for best business book about technology and the Carnegie Science Award in the Science Communicator category.

During Mickey’s tenure as CEO at MAYA the company won numerous Consumer Electronic Association (CEA) awards for product innovation, was selected multiple times as a top 20 “best small company to work for” in America by Fortune, Inc, and Entrepreneur magazines and spun-out, launched, or incubated five new MAYA organizations.

headline: On a data and marketing journey at BCG
about: Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

profileTopEducation.schoolName: Georgia Institute of Technology

experience.description: Member of BCG's Marketing, Sales & Pricing practice and BCG X.Growth, focused on marketing topics, such as, among others, strategic planning and allocation, execution and measurement, operations and processes

How do we take into consideration brand equity and relevant proxy KPIs (e.g., member activity) when doing marketing investment allocation? How do we take sports marketing into consideration? In this role I was tasked to bridge the measurement gap between different types of advertising investments, that are typically not included in short term MMM solutions. At the same time, I was leading key city (London, Paris and Berlin) marketing science analysts, and was responsible for coaching and unlocking full potential of all the managers in EMEA's marketing science team

A smart guy once said: insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results. Luckily, that’s not how we did things at Nike. I was leading a team focused on truly understanding the incrementality of our marketing efforts and the real power of our brand. On this journey, we were employing marketing mix modelling and multi-touch attribution to influence the strategy of EMEA’s Integrated Media team (brand media, performance social and display, search, affiliates) so that we would get the best bang for our buck

I was leading a team responsible for driving start-up like growth in EMEA by finding known and unknown unknowns (copyright by D. Rumsfeld, read more at https://www.kaushik.net/ ) and unlocking the full potential of Nike’s digital marketing team. Whether it’s search, media or social channels, we would look for patterns in consumer behaviour, try to identify the best investment opportunities and empower our leaders to make strategic business decisions through data-driven visual stories

As a member of EMEA’s Digital Analytics Team, I was dedicated to supporting Nike’s Performance Marketing team with reporting and analytics. I was using Adobe Analytics, SQL and Tableau on my “typical” day (no day is typical at Nike!) to understand how our marketing was performing, help improve our campaigns, and look for new growth opportunities within 39 countries

publications.title: A Monte-Carlo-Based Methodology for Determining the Fabrication Yield of Fibers for Lasers
publications.description: With the rapid progress of fiber lasers, there is increasing demand to develop optical waveguides providing large fundamental mode (FM) effective areas. Several of these fibers possess structural features, beyond the traditional core and cladding of a step-index fiber, in order to suppress higher-order modes (HOMs); however, their mode filtering capabilities are limited by imperfections in fabrication. In this work, we propose an approach based on Monte Carlo method that takes into account practical fabrication tolerances to determine the fabrication yields of complex fiber designs. Importantly, for a fiber design to be viable in applications, it must not only perform well optically, but also be robust against fabrication imperfections. We applied the methodology to an exemplary 33-μm W-type fiber, and assume independent uniform distributions of ±10% in all dimensions and numerical apertures (NAs). In total, 500 fabrication iterations are simulated, and the cumulative yield that simultaneously satisfies α FM <; 0.1 dB/m, α hom > 10 dB/m and A eff, fm > 400 μm 2 is found to be 21.6% ± 3.6% (95% confidence level) across coil radii between 10.2 cm and 27.0 cm. We expect this methodology to be particularly useful in predicting yields of fibers whose properties are based on resonant coupling (i.e. 3C and anti-resonant fibers), where imperfections in fabrication modify their resonance conditions.

publications.title: A tRNA modification in Mycobacterium tuberculosis facilitates optimal intracellular growth
publications.description: Diverse chemical modifications fine-tune the function and metabolism of tRNA. Although tRNA modification is universal, profiles of modifications, their functions, and physiological roles have not been elucidated in most organisms including the human pathogen, Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). To identify physiologically important modifications, we surveyed the tRNA of Mtb, using tRNA sequencing (tRNA-seq) and genome-mining. Homology searches identified 18 candidate tRNA modifying enzymes that are predicted to create 13 tRNA modifications across all tRNA species. Reverse transcription-derived error signatures in tRNA-seq predicted the sites and presence of 9 modifications. Several chemical treatments prior to tRNA-seq expanded the number of predictable modifications. Deletion of Mtb genes encoding two modifying enzymes, TruB and MnmA, eliminated their respective tRNA modifications, validating the presence of modified sites in tRNA species. Furthermore, the absence of mnmA attenuated Mtb growth in macrophages, suggesting that MnmA-dependent tRNA uridine sulfation contributes to Mtb intracellular growth. Our results lay the foundation for unveiling the roles of tRNA modifications in Mtb pathogenesis and developing new therapeutics against tuberculosis.

publications.title: Peptidyl tRNA hydrolase is required for robust prolyl-tRNA turnover in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
publications.description: Peptidyl tRNA hydrolase (Pth) is an enzyme that cuts unfinished peptides off tRNA that has been prematurely released from a stalled ribosome. Pth is essential in nearly all bacteria, including the pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), but it has not been clear why. We have used genetic and novel biochemical approaches to show that when Pth levels decline in Mtb, peptidyl tRNA accumulates to such an extent that usable tRNA pools drop. Thus, Pth is needed to maintain normal tRNA levels, most strikingly for prolyl-tRNAs. Many antibiotics act on protein synthesis and could be affected by altering the availability of tRNA. This is certainly true for tRNA synthetase inhibitors, several of which are drug candidates for tuberculosis. We find that their action is potentiated by Pth depletion. Furthermore, Pth depletion results in hypersensitivity to macrolides, drugs that are not active enough under ordinary circumstances to be useful for tuberculosis.

publications.title: Failing upwards: Genetics-based strategies to improve antibiotic discovery and efficacy in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
publications.publishedAt: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology · Sep 15, 2022
publications.description: Therapeutic advances in the 20th century significantly reduced tuberculosis (TB) mortality. Nonetheless, TB still poses a massive global health challenge with significant annual morbidity and mortality that has been amplified during the COVID-19 pandemic. Unlike most common bacterial infectious diseases, successful TB treatment requires months-long regimens, which complicates the ability to treat all cases quickly and effectively. Improving TB chemotherapy by reducing treatment duration and optimizing combinations of drugs is an important step to reducing relapse. In this review, we outline the limitations of current multidrug regimens against TB and have reviewed the genetic tools available to improve the identification of drug targets. The rational design of regimens that sterilize diverse phenotypic subpopulations will maximize bacterial killing while minimizing both treatment duration and infection relapse. Importantly, the TB field currently has all the necessary genetic and analytical tools to screen for and prioritize drug targets in vitro based on the vulnerability of essential and non-essential genes in the Mtb genome and to translate these findings in in vivo models. Combining genetic methods with chemical screens offers a formidable strategy to redefine the preclinical design of TB therapy by identifying powerful new targets altogether, as well as targets that lend new efficacy to existing drugs.

publications.title: A tRNA-acetylating toxin and detoxifying enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
publications.description: The global rise in antibiotic-resistant tuberculosis has prompted an urgent search for new drugs. Toxin-antitoxin (TA) systems allow bacteria to adapt rapidly to environmental changes, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis encodes more TA systems than any known pathogen. We have characterized a new TA system in M. tuberculosis: the toxin, TacT, acetylates charged tRNA to block protein synthesis. TacT's effects are reversed by the essential bacterial enzyme peptidyl tRNA hydrolase (Pth), which is currently being explored as an antibiotic target. Pth also cleaves peptidyl tRNAs that are prematurely released from stalled ribosomes. We assessed whether TacT modulates pth essentiality in M. tuberculosis because drugs targeting Pth might prompt resistance if TacT is disrupted. We show that pth essentiality is unaffected by the absence of this TA system, indicating that Pth's essential role hinges on its peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase activity. Our work underscores Pth's potential as a viable target for new antibiotics.

publications.title: The conserved translation factor LepA is required for optimal synthesis of a porin family in Mycobacterium smegmatis
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Bacteriology (American Society for Microbiology) · Dec 23, 2020
publications.description: The mycobacterial cell wall is a promising target for new antibiotics due to the abundance of important membrane-associated proteins. Defining mechanisms of synthesis of the membrane proteome will be critical to uncovering and validating drug targets. We found that LepA, a universally conserved translation factor, controls the synthesis of a number of major membrane proteins in M. smegmatis. LepA primarily controls synthesis of the major porin MspA. Loss of LepA results in decreased permeability through the loss of this porin, including permeability to antibiotics like rifampin and vancomycin. In mycobacteria, regulation from the ribosome is critical for the maintenance of membrane homeostasis and, importantly, antibiotic susceptibility.

publications.title: A bacterial riboswitch class for the thiamin precursor HMP-PP employs a terminator-embedded aptamer
publications.description: We recently implemented a bioinformatics pipeline that can uncover novel, but rare, riboswitch candidates as well as other noncoding RNA structures in bacteria. A prominent candidate revealed by our initial search efforts was called the ‘thiS motif’ because of its frequent association with a gene coding for the ThiS protein, which delivers sulfur to form the thiazole moiety of the thiamin precursor HET-P. In the current report, we describe biochemical and genetic data demonstrating that thiS motif RNAs function as sensors of the thiamin precursor HMP-PP, which is fused with HET-P ultimately to form the final active coenzyme thiamin pyrophosphate (TPP). HMP-PP riboswitches exhibit a distinctive architecture wherein an unusually small ligand-sensing aptamer is almost entirely embedded within an otherwise classic intrinsic transcription terminator stem. This arrangement yields remarkably compact genetic switches that bacteria use to tune the levels of thiamin precursors during the biosynthesis of this universally distributed coenzyme.

publications.title: Challenges of ligand identification for the second wave of orphan riboswitch candidates
publications.description: Orphan riboswitch candidates are noncoding RNA motifs whose representatives are believed to function as genetic regulatory elements, but whose target ligands have yet to be identified. The study of certain orphans, particularly classes that have resisted experimental validation for many years, has led to the discovery of important biological pathways and processes once their ligands were identified. Previously, we highlighted details for four of the most common and intriguing orphan riboswitch candidates. This facilitated the validation of riboswitches for the signaling molecules c-di-AMP, ZTP, and ppGpp, the metal ion Mn2+, and the metabolites guanidine and PRPP. Such studies also yield useful linkages between the ligands sensed by the riboswitches and numerous biochemical pathways. In the current report, we describe the known characteristics of 30 distinct classes of orphan riboswitch candidates – some of which have remained unsolved for over a decade. We also discuss the prospects for uncovering novel biological insights via focused studies on these RNAs. Lastly, we make recommendations for experimental objectives along the path to finding ligands for these mysterious RNAs.

publications.title: Inhibition of ErbB3 by a monoclonal antibody that locks the extracellular domain in an inactive configuration
publications.publishedAt: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) · Oct 1, 2015
publications.description: ErbB3 (HER3) is a member of the EGF receptor (EGFR) family of receptor tyrosine kinases, which, unlike the other three family members, contains a pseudo kinase in place of a tyrosine kinase domain. In cancer, ErbB3 activation is driven by a ligand-dependent mechanism through the formation of heterodimers with EGFR, ErbB2, or ErbB4 or via a ligand-independent process through heterodimerization with ErbB2 overexpressed in breast tumors or other cancers. Here we describe the crystal structure of the Fab fragment of an antagonistic monoclonal antibody KTN3379, currently in clinical development in human cancer patients, in complex with the ErbB3 extracellular domain. The structure reveals a unique allosteric mechanism for inhibition of ligand-dependent or ligand-independent ErbB3-driven cancers by binding to an epitope that locks ErbB3 in an inactive conformation. Given the similarities in the mechanism of ErbB receptor family activation, these findings could facilitate structure-based design of antibodies that inhibit EGFR and ErbB4 by an allosteric mechanism.

experience.description: Patrick partners with leaders and organizations to drive transformational talent outcomes through upskilling and learning. He has deep experience in the topic, both as a consultant and advisor with BCG, and as a former start-up executive in the ed tech space. He is passionate about helping companies shape and deliver on their talent strategies, leveraging innovative learning and upskilling techniques to maximize human potential within organizations.

Section is creating the business upskilling platform of the future. Using their proprietary sprint format, they partner with world-class business school professors to deliver high-quality business education that drives real-world outcomes. 

As Enterprise Business Lead, I was responsible for managing a portfolio of enterprise accounts and the customer success managers who served them. I worked directly with senior learning and business leaders at our clients, which included small and medium sized business teams, as well as teams from marquee global brands like L'Oreal, Unilever, and Microsoft. Given the entrepreneurial stage of the company, I was deeply involved across functions on anything touching enterprise, from marketing and sales, to product, to operations, and of course to renewals and account growth.

Guild is on a mission to unlock opportunity for America’s workforce through education and upskilling, with a double bottom-line business model that does well by doing good. Guild works with leading Fortune 1000 employers such as The Walt Disney Company, Walmart, Discover, Chipotle and Lowe's to transform their education & upskilling programs through Guild's technology platform, payments system and learning marketplace. With nearly 800 employees and a growing customer base, Guild is a fast-growing company that was recognized as a winner of Fast Company’s 2020 World Changing Ideas award and a CNBC Disruptor 50 company for its work at the intersection of education and the future of work. 

As a Client Services Principal, I served and managed key enterprise accounts, ensuring that Guild's offering was delivering on the business and learning objectives they set out. I was privileged to be part of the core CS team serving Walmart, a long-standing partner of Guild's.

Society is transitioning from an industrial economy to a knowledge economy where success is driven by higher-order problem solving, continuous learning, and deep domain expertise. But, despite this radical shift, education has not kept pace. 

Too many are being left behind: low-income, first-generation and adult learners; the thirty million people with debt but no degree; the truck drivers and others soon to be automated out of a job. And the surfeit of students who have completed degrees but earn no more than high school graduates. 

We must aggressively pursue new, scaled learning solutions that support all learners in acquiring and signaling the skills and capabilities they need to flourish and provide for themselves. This imperative requires an ecosystem approach leveraging the abilities and expertise of entrepreneurs, universities, foundations, companies and government.

Entangled is an ecosystem approach to an ecosystem problem. We work across boundaries to harvest insights and unlock capacities of people and organizations poised to accelerate innovation, foster equity, and create commercial opportunity in education.

As a Project Leader at BCG, I've worked primarily with mission-driven companies in the education and health care industries on core strategic topics. I have also spent time as an Ambassador to BCG's think tank, The Bruce Henderson Institute, working with senior BCG leaders on the challenges and opportunities related to learning and talent development in the digital age.

I've managed diverse teams and have worked with BCGers across functions, industries, and geographies. Managers at BCG are responsible for the case's intellectual agenda, leading collaborative teams to deliver against ambitious client objectives. Being a PL is part problem solving and analysis, part communication, part project and program management, part stakeholder management.

A sampling of my experience as a PL includes:

-Performing a private school market evaluation for a major school operator in Middle East ahead, evaluating multiple countries' markets for size, trends, risks, competitor analysis, and client positioning
-Counseling the Board, CEO, and President of leading, mission-driven med tech company on Board-level strategic, operational, and organizational issues, in seven-month advisory / “chief of staff” role
-Managing relationships with BCG's own digital learning partners, including universities and Coursera, in the creation of multiple BCG-branded digital learning assets
-Driving the firm's learning and talent development research and business agenda through work with BCG's think tank, The Bruce Henderson Institute

As a consultant at BCG, I worked primarily in the health care and public sector industries, and spent time in our Chicago, Dubai, and San Francisco offices.

Consultants provide the intellectual and analytical horsepower for our core client work, supporting with every aspect of case execution, from up-front scoping of work, to framing and structuring of approach, to research and gathering of key data points, to execution of analysis, to stakeholder engagement and communication of findings.

-Assessing the proposed establishment of children’s hospital for a U.S. state university health system. I helped design and manage the financial model for merger of multiple children’s care units into stand-alone entity, working across hospital types (for-profit, non-profit university, and non-profit religiously affiliate)

Is Your Upskilling Program Paying Off
publications.description:
Contrary to popular belief, calculating the return on upskilling program investments is in fact possible. BCG’s three-step approach requires companies to:
1. Identify the desired business impact upfront. This step is crucial for ensuring that the program’s goals support the company’s business strategy and people objectives.
2. Define the metrics for holding the program accountable to that impact and measuring progress. Metrics that capture the end results should take priority, but those that monitor progress made in the course of a program are also important.
3. Determine whether the targeted impact has been achieved. The importance of the program and the expectations of leaders will determine how rigorous the assessment should be.

Outside of work, you’ll likely find me cooking something ambitious, rock climbing somewhere vertical, or playing chess.

headline: Senior Partner and Managing Director; Global co-Leader, Sports segment at Boston Consulting Group (BCG)
about:
I am a Senior Partner and Managing Director for Boston Consulting Group.  I joined BCG in 1995 in Sydney and have served in Chicago since 2001. I am the founder & global co-leader of BCG's Sports sector; I have completed a successful full term as the global leader of BCG’s Consumer & Retail practice (2019-25).

My experience covers two areas of focus and depth:

1 - Consumer: Have led &/or been core to several of BCG’s global, marquee, sustained, highest client value-creating relationships. Categories covered include snacking, beverages, alcohol, home & personal care, restaurants, apparel and durables. Have covered the full spectrum of business issues with particular depth on issues of corporate strategy & transformation, consumer-driven brand strategy (including co-founding and leading BCG's differentiated Demand-Centric Growth capability) and commercial growth. 
 
2 - Sport: Have served a broad spectrum of the marquee / leading  governing bodies, leagues, teams, major events, media and PE, across six continents and across most major sports. I have a track record of developing & enabling breakthrough actions and impact in these organizations, with many of those visible and enduring in the sporting ecosystem today. 

I hold a Master of Management from Northwestern University (Kellogg), a Master of Philosophy in International Relations from the University of Cambridge, UK and a Bachelor of Business with the University Medal from the University of Technology, Sydney.

I have played two sports at an elite level (Cricket in England & Field Hockey in Australia), am a published author (Rocket - on Consumer marketing), a film Executive Producer (Doosra - a socio-sports film currently in production) and a Founder’s Circle member for the America India Foundation.

Versatile manager, strategy, and value creation professional with 7+ years of working experience:
At Boston Consulting Group (BCG), I’ve developed strong expertise in strategic problem-solving, operational improvements, and driving value creation across industrial and private equity sectors. I’ve worked closely with global industrial leaders and private equity clients to deliver meaningful results, combining deep analysis with practical execution.

During my time at Cornerstone Research, I led teams of 5-10 analysts to craft case strategies, conduct thorough research, and deliver actionable insights. headline: Senior Partner and Managing Director of BCG's Great Lakes System
about:
I am a Senior Partner and Managing Director for the Boston Consulting Group. I lead BCG's Great Lakes System of offices encompassing Chicago, Detroit, and Minneapolis. I also serve on the leadership team for the Marketing Sale and Pricing Practice Area and was previously the Global Lead for Sales and Go-to-Market and Head of the Chicago Office.

I work across consumer, retail and industrial goods B2B clients with a strong focus on distribution businesses. My work is focused on large transformations,growth, turnarounds, and major programs across a wide range of industries. My work spans category management, sales, organizational design, operations, and pricing 

Prior to BCG, I worked in a variety of strategy and marketing roles at Target and Safeway.

I hold a BA from University of Notre Dame and an MBA from University of Chicago. I serve as a board member for BCG's Center for Illinois Future (CIF) and am a member of Civic Committee of Chicago.

publications.title: A Circular Future for Glass
publications.description:
Glass is infinitely recyclable, capable of being continually reused without a loss in quality or purity. It is one of the reasons that consumers know and trust glass. Yet the US does not recycle nearly as much glass as it could. The country’s glass-recycling rate has hovered around 33% for many years. In Europe and some US states with bottle deposit laws, average glass-recycling rates are closer to 70%—proof that high rates of glass recycling are possible.

The Glass Packaging Institute has partnered with Boston Consulting Group to develop a ten-year plan to raise the US’s glass recycling rate to 50%. The plan has three pillars:
1) Leave no bottle behind. This multiprong initiative involves new or expanded bottle-bill laws, clean collection options, and expanded commercial recycling programs.
2) Transform the recycling system. Investments and improvements must be made in collection, separating, and processing, especially in selected regions, to reduce the glass that is carted to landfills.
3) Drive collective action. This entails creating user-friendly deposit-return programs run by the private sector and other cooperative approaches that build awareness and momentum.

These pillars are self-reinforcing. Improving collection rates without investing in sorting and processing infrastructure, for example, would not fundamentally improve the recycling rate, and vice versa. A comprehensive approach is necessary.

In 2021, recycling is not optional. Recovering a material that can be recycled forever makes economic and environmental sense, helping to achieve global sustainability and greenhouse gas reduction goals. The Glass Packaging Institute is committed to unlocking the full potential and innate circularity of glass by forming industry, consumer, and public partnerships to achieve a 50% glass recycling rate by 2030.

publications.title: Your Supply Chain Needs a Sustainability Strategy
publications.description:
As economies reopen following the damage wrought by COVID-19, businesses are rethinking their operations, seeking to transform themselves into more nimble and resilient organizations. This is, in fact, an historic opportunity for companies to “build back better.”

Leading organizations are focusing particularly closely on their global supply chains. They are striving to enhance their supply chains’ agility and efficiency. Critically, these organizations are also working to improve their supply chains’ sustainability (as well as the sustainability of their supply chain partners), often experimenting with unprecedented types of collaborations with suppliers, customers, and even competitors across sectors and geographies. The companies have concluded that these extra efforts are a high-payback investment, since greener supply chains can deliver benefits for both business and the environment.

Here we present our broader argument for greener supply chains. We think you’ll find it compelling.

For example, when reviewing the pump hydraulics, I noticed that the design conditions for any given line were always coincident (maximum pressure and normal temperature or maximum temperature and normal pressure) however did not report maximum pressure and temperature, which was feasible for some lines during an upset and may be required for lines registered with ABSA. This resulted in a full review of the line list to determine the impact on the line list (for example changes in flange ratings) if maximum pressure and temperature were used as the required design conditions. I also identified early in the project that the FEED minimum design temperature used was -46°C rather than -45°C which means that a different classification is required for the equipment or a custom deviation will need to be requested from every vendor for each piece of equipment. As such, this concern was raised to the mechanical team and they modified all of the equipment bids to have a minimum temperature of -45°C rather than -46°C. Being in this role exposed me to skills required for becoming a lead (especially in brownfield project) when it is vital to constantly monitor the entire scope and question how every change / decision has a cascading effect on the remainder of the scope.

The LNGC Phase 2 Optimization study consisted of reviewing 3 utility systems that utilize the main pipe racks (Thermal Heating Fluid, hypochlorite and vapor return from the jetties) to determine if the lines for each process train can be merged / optimized to create space in the main pipe rack or to take advantage of excess pipe that was purchased in Phase 1. With such a small scope and the lead fully occupied with Phase 1, this project allowed me to behave as the Process point of contact and developer of scope. 
From the initial project request I: 
•	Collected project documentation (for example P&IDs and system descriptions) to gain a full picture of the three utilities and determined how they were designed in Phase 1. 
•	Created high level sketches that incorporated Phase 1 and Phase 2 scope and used the sketches to determine the required modifications that would be required to merge the system lines and optimize space in the pipe rack. I also 
•	Talked to the Phase 1 process leads of each area to ensure that there weren’t gaps in my understanding of the systems (for example did line sizes have a maximum limit due to velocity requirement or was there only a minimum line size requirement for hydraulics) 
•	Proposed a final recommendation for each system. 
These recommendations were written up as a supplement to the overall study report and I was the point of contact for any client questions that arose from the recommendations. The process lead was informed throughout this project so that he could provide any feedback as well make sure he didn’t feel like he was surprised with any decisions.

As part of the Mining Hot Water Production Challenge for COSIA and Foresight, I evaluated the impact of CO2 emission reduction when using Submerged Combustion from Inproheat or flue gas cooling from C&ES in lieu of steam to heat recycle water in an oil sands mine facility. The responsibilities included:

The model was created to extract the information generated by Inproheat and C&ES and quickly evaluated the cases with minimal manual input The model is intended to be simple so that it can be easily run by the client in the future.

projects.title: Cube-It - A Conversational Experience to Help People Learn About Each Other
projects.associatedWith: Associated with IIT Institute of Design
projects.description:
We live in a time that celebrates virtual communication. We are always checking our phone. There might be 500 Facebook accounts we befriended with and 1,000 Instagram followers who scrolled over our ‘story’ every day, but when was the last time you had an actual conversation with someone? One that is face to face, one that stays in your head, one that really makes you have a deeper connection with someone and know that person better afterward. 

It is also the time that virtual assistants expand their existence and engagement in our lives. From Siri, Alexa to Google home, talking and chatting to a bot is becoming a natural behavior. So far, our interaction with these voice interfaces are task-oriented - bots are helping human to complete a task, even if the request is ‘tell me a bad joke’. What if the virtual assistant could act as a facilitator for human’s conversation? That is what Cube-it offers - an experiential space to help people build stronger bonds by leveraging artificial conversational technologies. It creates an intimate experience of conversation for friends, couples, and families who are interested in developing a deeper connection.

receivedRecommendations.description:
I’ve had the privilege of working with Ran across several projects, and I can say without hesitation: he’s one of the most thoughtful, helpful, strategic, and creatively sharp people I’ve collaborated with.

Ran brings a rare ability to navigate between the macro and micro — shaping product vision while sweating the details that make experiences truly work. Whether he’s mapping complex service journeys, aligning cross-functional teams, or translating messy problem spaces into clear product direction, he does it all with curiosity, clarity, and heart. 

What stands out most is how he leads with empathy — not just for users, but for his teammates. He listens deeply, challenges thoughtfully, and always keeps the focus on impact.

As someone who moves seamlessly between product, design and strategic design, Ran brings the clarity and creativity you need when you're navigating ambiguity and trying to turn ideas into real, meaningful outcomes. 

If you're building something meaningful and want to make it a joy along the way — Ran’s your person

receivedRecommendations.givenAt: February 9, 2025, Jenny worked with Ran on the same team
receivedRecommendations.description:
I’ve worked with Ran on multiple projects over the past three years, and he’s hands down one of the best researchers and product strategists I know. He has a way of asking the right questions, uncovering key insights, and pushing for decisions that actually make a difference.

What really makes Ran stand out is that he’s the kind of person you always want in your corner. Even outside of the projects we worked on together, whenever I’ve had questions about my own work—whether I needed a second pair of eyes, wasn’t sure if we were thinking about something the right way, or just felt like we might be missing something—I’d ping Ran. And every time, he’d offer a fresh perspective, ask a question I hadn’t considered, or just help me think things through.

He’s also an incredibly supportive leader. He gives thoughtful, constructive feedback and genuinely cares about the people he works with. I’ve learned so much from him, and I’d absolutely love to work with him again in the future. If you ever get the chance to work with Ran, take it. You won’t regret it.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: I guide teams that make products people love.  Product Design • Design Management • Design Strategy • User Research • Service Design
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: February 21, 2024, Paul managed Ran directly
receivedRecommendations.description:
I worked with Ran for the first time when he was still relatively new to high-intensity consulting, and I was not sure what to expect from this soft-spoken researcher assigned to my team.

I quickly learned that I could trust Ran completely as we traveled to multiple customer sites of our client to conduct contextual inquiry that would help us to create a new product offering. These interactions often involved brash, no-nonsense people wary about why we needed to know so much about their operations. Despite working in a non-native language, Ran built rapport, asked insightful questions, and exhibited a sharp eye for noticing details.

In addition to research expertise, we ended up tapping Ran for interface concept design and wire framing as well—plus, he created the foundation for our underlying information architecture.

He ended up owning so many aspects of this project that it totally made sense for him to own the client presentations as well, taking senior leaders through the work, conveying the value and implications for the follow-on product-development effort.

In the years since, I've seen from afar this same fail-safe competence and proactive willingness to dive in when he has taken on many other internal and external projects.

Ran also has so much to offer the world as a genuinely joyful, empathetic humanist (well . . . and “catist”) who also regularly introduces colleagues to memorably mind-blowing cuisine.

I can only cross my fingers hoping I will have a chance to work with him again.

about:
A hands-on engineering leader with a 15-year track record of developing complex technology solutions for Fortune 500 companies. Deep expertise in Software development, AI, Cloud computing, IoT, and Data Engineering. Demonstrates a strong ability to define solution architectures, build effective engineering teams, and execute strategic technology roadmaps, with a focus on delivering measurable business results.

Experience Highlights:

• Fleet monitoring system: Designed & developed a near real-time fleet monitoring system, processing vast amounts of IoT data to provide actionable insights & improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) by 10% using Spark Structured Streaming.

• B2B E-commerce Platform: Built a B2B e-commerce platform using Micro-services architecture, integrating multiple existing ERP and CRM systems resulting in increased customer LTV, higher order volumes & reducing manual effort. Scaled the platform to 5 business units of the OEM.

• Document processing engine: Built a document processing engine using Azure Cognitive services and OCR to extract data from customized PDF documents (Bill of Materials). Significantly enhanced user experience when searching & ordering replacement parts for industrial machines leading to increased order volumes.

• IoT Gateway Automation: Designed and led the development of a web-based machine IoT gateway configuration tool for an OEM, significantly reducing onboarding time (from a week to just an hour) and manual entry errors.

• Process optimization using Gen AI: Identified high value GenAI use cases & led the development of GenAI solution for a major US insurance firm, reducing claim processing time from two weeks to just four hours. 

• Demand Forecasting: Led the enhancement & roll-out of an in-house demand forecasting engine for a global fast food chain, resulting in increase in annual sales by $50M.

• Client & Stakeholder Management: Successfully managed client engagements and relationships (direct reports to the CxOs). Collaborated with business teams to define project scope, deliverables, timelines, while managing stakeholder/sponsor communication and expectations.

• Leadership: Led 50 people org with cross functional teams across software engineering, data science, product & design on large-scale multi-year digital transformation projects and managed budgets up to $75M.

• Talent Management & Development: Actively involved in recruiting, performance reviews, and mentorship for engineering staff for North & South America.

publications.title: How Big Consumer Companies Can Fight Back
publications.description:
Small brands are stealing share from big brands. Consumers are applying Caudalie skin cream after their morning shower, drinking Peet’s coffee and eating Chobani yogurt at breakfast, visiting Pret A Manger for lunch, and winding down in the evening with a Ballast Point craft beer. 

Conventional wisdom says that today’s consumers want healthy, natural food and personal-care options, and millennials, in particular, prefer authentic to mass-produced goods. To win back this new breed of consumer, the thinking goes, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies have few options. Either they can launch small brands, at the risk of fragmenting attention and resources, or they can try to increase earnings through deep cost cutting, emulating the approach the private equity firm 3G Capital has taken in its acquisitions of large consumer brands. In short, many believe organic growth from the core is over. 

We disagree.

publications.title: Demand-Centric Growth: How to Grow by Finding Out What Really Drives Consumer Choice
publications.description: This article is the second in a series based on Rocket: Eight Lessons to Secure Infinite Growth, which tells the stories of 16 business leaders who created iconic brands. The book, by Michael Silverstein, Dylan Bolden, Rune Jacobsen, and Rohan Sajdeh, is available now.

publications.title: Which Companies Drove U.S. CPG Growth in 2014?
publications.description: For many manufacturers of consumer packaged goods (CPGs), 2014 was an elusive year for growth. Sluggishness, uncertainty, and concerns over jobs and wages dogged the domestic economy for much of the year. In tough circumstances, some companies outperformed while others lagged. What drove the leaders’ success?

publications.title: An Imperative For Consumer Companies To Go Green: When Social Responsibility Leads to Growth
publications.description:
Goods labeled organic, natural, ecological, and fair trade are no longer a niche in the food, personal-care, and household products sectors. These goods have entered mainstream retailers and become a large part of the market, with a broad base of consumers now purchasing them. In an otherwise stagnant industry, these “responsible consumption” (RC) products represent a major area of profitable growth.

The Boston Consulting Group has worked with market research company Information Resources Inc. to analyze point-of-sale data from nearly all retail chains in the U.S. (grocery, convenience, department, and wholesale-club stores). Not only do RC products account for 15 percent of all sales in these chains but also sales have grown about 9 percent annually in the past three years—making up 70 percent of total growth. Similar turnover and growth levels are expected across developed markets. Global surveys point to future growth as well, as most consumers intend to expand the number of categories in which they seek out RC products.

publications.title: Who Are the Growth Leaders in U.S. Consumer Packaged Goods?
publications.description:
For the second year, BCG and Information Resources, Inc. have ranked more than 400 consumer-packaged-goods companies, both public and private, to identify winners among small, midsize, and large players.
 
Small companies continue to take market share from large companies, a trend that has been ongoing for the past several years.
 
Some top-performing large companies are bucking that trend, in part by finding ways to generate growth from their base businesses.

publications.title: Elevate Your Marketing Measurement: The Four-Legged Approach to Understanding Marketing ROI
publications.description:
Marketing spend is often labelled as a cost center, especially when budgets tighten. But with the right measurement strategy, it can be a powerful profit driver.
 
In our latest @BCG X blog, we dive into the complexities of marketing measurement and introduce a “Four-Legged” approach, designed to provide a comprehensive and accurate view of marketing ROI. By combining methodologies like modeling, incrementality experiments, customer insights, and execution metrics, it can help marketeers transform marketing from a perceived cost center into a demonstrable profit opportunity.

publications.title: How Nimble CMOs Invest Their Marketing Budgets
Companies Gain When CMOs and CFOs Measure Success Together
publications.description: Measurement is fundamental to business, starting with the reporting of profit and loss. But when it comes to marketing investments, choosing which metrics to track can be a challenge. Finance and marketing often clash on this point. The two functions have different points of view, each rooted in its own corporate silo. They also tend to speak different languages, or at least use different nomenclatures, which makes aligning on a common system difficult.

publications.title: Climate Targets 2030: How Switzerland Can Halve Its Domestic Greenhouse Gas Emissions
publications.description:
Switzerland faces an enormous climate challenge. By 2030, under the Paris Agreement, the country must reduce its annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by at least 50 percent compared to 1990 levels. Two-thirds of these reductions must be achieved in the next eight years, while only one-third has been achieved between 1990 and 2021. Switzerland has also the potential to become a pioneer in the fight against climate change. The Swiss economy is considered the most innovative in the world, leading universities in climate science and globally leading climate start-ups are based in Switzerland. 
The decarbonization of the transport, building, industry and agriculture sectors and the required expansion of renewable energies will need additional investments totaling around 140 billion Swiss francs by 2030.

publications.title: Future of Distribution in Europe
publications.description: Technological advancement has brought about disruptive change to European insurance markets – and the pandemic has undoubtedly accelerated this trend. While many struggle to keep up with changing customer preferences and the evolving competitive and regulatory landscapes, the market leaders of tomorrow are eager to anticipate market developments and are taking the right steps today to conquer the new realities of the future. Distribution in insurance might be one of those areas where all signs point to a shift in the market dynamics, driven by rapid change in several dimensions. Traditional players need to find their place in this changing landscape – and technology, data, and analytics provide them with just the right tools to do so. This paper highlights ways for insurers to take embrace the new future in distribution.

As companies pivot to more sustainable value creation models, they need to make sure that their investors understand the changes that will take place and the thinking behind them. TSR has no memory. publications.title: Steinzeit Teilzeit - Schweizer Unternehmen müssen ihr Potential nutzen
publications.description: Die Schweiz hat grossen Aufholbedarf. Unsere Teilzeitmodelle sind verstaubt oder inexistent und Frauen wie Männer leiden unter den starren Rastern unserer Unternehmen und den Vorstellungen der Nachbarn und Arbeitskollegen. In der Schweiz bleiben heute geschätzte 50’000 Akademikerinnen zu Hause. Dies ist eine äusserst unbefriedigende Situation. So kann die Schweizer Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft nicht mehr vom Wissen und dem Engagement dieser hochqualifizierten Frauen profitieren. Zudem fliesst das Geld, das der Staat in deren Ausbildung investiert hat, rund 5,75 Mrd. Fr., nicht mehr in den Wirtschaftskreislauf zurück. Mit der Diskussion zur Begrenzung der Zuwanderung ausländischer Arbeitskräfte erhält diese Thematik nun frischen Schub. Hiesige Unternehmen werden künftig weniger ausländische Fachkräfte rekrutieren können. Der von Unternehmen schon länger monierte Fachkräftemangel wird sich weiter verschärfen. Die Mobilisierung von heute nicht erwerbstätigen, aber bestens ausgebildeten Frauen wird hier eine entscheidende Rolle spielen.

publications.title: Creative Switzerland? Fostering an Innovation Powerhouse
publications.description: In light of the increasing mobility of multinational companies, and escalating competitiveness to attract those companies, Switzerland needs to promote its most important advantage – a creative environment for innovation – in order to continue to attract and retain these companies. This study calls for action that will enable Switzerland to do just that and thereby sustain its competitive advantage in the global economy. Clearly, a multinational company with significant innovation activities in Switzerland, which creates above average value for the Swiss economy, is less likely to relocate than a management holding company. Innovative industries contribute more than a third of Swiss GDP and, over the past ten years, grew more than twice as fast as other industries in Switzerland. Multinational companies play a vital role in these innovative industries. Switzerland needs to take the necessary political action to increase its competitiveness in promoting itself as the best place for innovation. This study describes five critical initiatives for doing so.

publications.title: Experimental metrics for detection of detailed balance violation
publications.description: We report on the measurement of detailed balance violation in a coupled, noise-driven linear electronic circuit consisting of two nominally identical RC elements that are coupled via a variable capacitance. The state variables are the time-dependent voltages across each of the two primary capacitors, and the system is driven by independent noise sources in series with each of the resistances. From the recorded time histories of these two voltages, we quantify violations of detailed balance by three methods: (1) explicit construction of the probability current density, (2) constructing the time-dependent stochastic area, and (3) constructing statistical fluctuation loops. In comparing the three methods, we find that the stochastic area is relatively simple to implement and computationally inexpensive and provides a highly sensitive means for detecting violations of detailed balance.

publications.title: The Germline and Somatic Origins of Prostate Cancer Heterogeneity
publications.description:
We analyzed whole genomes from 666 prostate tumors to explore how inherited (germline) and acquired (somatic) mutations shape prostate cancer evolution. We uncovered 223 recurrently mutated driver regions and found that germline variants influence the emergence of specific somatic drivers. Our results show that high-grade tumors carry more aggressive mutations and evolve early, helping to predict relapse risk.

I am a co-author of this study.

publications.title: Genomic evolution shapes prostate cancer disease type
publications.description:
This study investigated how prostate cancers evolve by analyzing genomic data from localized tumors. We identified two distinct evolutionary trajectories, Canonical and Alternative, based on patterns of genetic alterations. Our findings revealed that tumors can be grouped into "evotypes" with distinct disease behaviors, offering a unified framework to study disease progression and potential treatment strategies.

I am a co-author of this study.

publications.title: Estimation of tumor cell total mRNA expression in 15 cancer types predicts disease progression
publications.description:
This work outlines a new approach to quantify tumor-specific mRNA levels from patient tumor samples (which contain both cancer and non-cancer cells). By applying this approach to tumors from >6,500 patients, we show that higher mRNA levels in cancer cells were associated with reduced patient survival.

I am a co-author of this study.

publications.title: Quantifying the influence of mutation detection on tumour subclonal reconstruction
publications.description:
Many algorithms have been developed to evaluate how cancers change over time but the variation across different algorithms is largely unknown. We evaluated sixteen pipelines for reconstructing how cancers evolve over time. This work highlights consistencies and differences across algorithms should help cancer researchers better understand the biases in their methods and design better studies.

I am a co-lead author of this study.

publications.title: Divergent mutational processes distinguish hypoxic and normoxic tumours
publications.description:
Many cancers have low levels of oxygen (hypoxia) and hypoxic tumours respond poorly to therapy. Here, as part of the ICGC/TCGA Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes (PCAWG) Consortium, which aggregated whole genome sequencing data from 2,658 cancers across 38 tumour types, we quantify hypoxia in 1,188 tumours spanning 27 cancer types. Elevated hypoxia was associated with increased mutational load across cancer types, irrespective of underlying mutational class. Overall, this represents the broadest genomic evaluation of hypoxia across cancers to date.

I am the lead author of this study.

publications.title: Pan-cancer analysis of whole genomes
publications.description:
A landmark publication describing the genetic analysis of >2,600 cancers spanning 38 tumor types.

I was a member of The ICGC/TCGA Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes Consortium (the international group carrying out this study).

publications.title: Widespread and functional RNA circularization in localized prostate cancer
publications.description:
Messenger RNA (mRNA) molecules play important roles in health and disease. Most studies of mRNAs have studied these molecules in their linear form. However, many mRNAs can be circular rather than linear. Circular RNAs can be more stable and may accordingly be better for biomarker development. We performed the largest study to date of circular RNAs in prostate cancer samples from patients and evaluated their potential utility as biomarkers for aggressive disease.

I am a co-author of this study

publications.title: Molecular landmarks of tumor hypoxia across cancer types
publications.description:
Many cancers have low levels of oxygen (hypoxia) and hypoxic cancers are known to be more aggressive. However, our understanding of the genetics associated with hypoxia has been limited. To address this, we examined hypoxia in over 8,000 tumours from 19 different cancer types. We found several common genetic markers of hypoxia across cancer types. We also developed an integrative biomarker that highlights patients who may benefit from more treatment. Overall, this represents the most comprehensive genomic analysis of hypoxia in cancer to date.

I am the lead author of this study.

publications.title: Development and validation of a 28-gene hypoxia-related prognostic signature for localized prostate cancer
publications.description:
We identified genes regulated by hypoxia (low oxygen) in prostate cancer cell lines. Using these genes we then developed a biomarker that predicts patient outcome. The biomarker was able to identify patients with poor and favourable outcome in 11 independent cohorts.

I am a co-author of this study.

publications.title: Prediction of overall survival for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: development of a prognostic model through a crowdsourced challenge with open clinical trial data.
publications.description:

I am a part of the Prostate Cancer Challenge DREAM Community (co-author).

publications.title: A Prostate Cancer “Nimbosus”: Genomic Instability and SChLAP1 Dysregulation Underpin Aggression of Intraductal and Cribriform Subpathologies
publications.description:
We identified genomic and tumour microenvironmental features associated with aggressive sub-pathologies in prostate cancer (intraductal carcinoma and cribriform architecture). We also proposed the concept of a tumour "nimbosus" (gathering of stormy clouds, Latin), where the culmination of several aggressive features leads to increased metastatic capacity and lethality.

I am a co-author of this study.

publications.title: Comparing continuous and discrete analyses of breast cancer survival information
publications.description:
We assessed differences between two commonly used statistical models in cancer using nearly 2,000 breast cancer samples. We then used machine learning to develop a hybrid methodology, which used both statistical models, and demonstrated the superiority of this approach.

I am the lead author of this study.

publications.title: "Investments in telecom infrastructure is gaining momentum"
publications.description:
More and more investors from the fields of infrastructure and commercial real estate are choosing to invest in communications infrastructures such as fiber optics, cellular networks, data centers and more. At the same time, telecom companies in Israel and abroad are looking to add such investors into their investments in the deployment of telecom infrastructure.

This trend, according to TASC experts, is projected to gain more momentum in the upcoming years:

- The need for communications infrastructure is growing at a tremendous rate
- Investing in communications infrastructure requires high volumes of capital for a long-term investment
- Joint venture of telecom player (which is more operational in its characteristics and capital structure) together with a long-term investor provides several advantages for both sides (by decreasing capital costs, increasing motivation for other teleco's to use the infrastructure and a better risks' mitigation)

However, Investors should examine several factors before entering such a JV (such as price and volume agreements with the Telecom partner, policy regarding wholesale selling, competitive landscape etc.)

publications.description:
La selección de artículos y traducciones recoge importantes contribuciones en distintas áreas de la filosofía agrupadas en tres grandes temas que han sido, además, los principales ejes temáticos en los números de la revista: experiencia, lenguaje y sociedad. El libro cuenta tanto con artículos inéditos como con traducciones hechas, en su mayoría, por personas que alguna vez fueron integrantes de Saga.
 
Así, en la primera sección, se encuentran, por una parte, las traducciones de los artículos de Maxine Sheets Johnstone, Dan Zahavi y David Chalmers, y, por otra, la contribución inédita de Søren Overgaard. La segunda, dedicada al lenguaje, está conformada por los artículos de Graham Priest, Hubert Marraud, Raúl Meléndez y Luciano Floridi. Finalmente, la última sección cuenta con una traducción del artículo de Sally Haslanger y un artículo inédito de Jon Elster.

headline: BCG | Kellogg MBA | University of Chicago
about:
I'm Gustavo Andrés Grau Bolívar, originally from Caracas, Venezuela, and an Analyst for Charles River Associates, working under the Antitrust and Competition Economics practice in Chicago.

I have experience in academic research working for both Prof. John List and Prof. Steven Levitt at the Becker-Friedman Institute studying behavioral economics and human capital. In the finance industry I have been a financial analyst at Cidel Financial Group. There, I evaluated alternative investment strategies, and that experience propelled me further into the world of hedge funds, investment banks, and private equity firms. Consequently, I founded an educational program on investment theory and practice within my business fraternity. It has grown to over 25 members and will be an integral part of the fraternity the following years.

When I'm not in school, I enjoy playing soccer and basketball. At home, I'm an amateur cook who enjoys traveling to experience new food, cultures, and languages.

headline: Principal at Boston Consulting Group (BCG) | Consumer, Medtech, Operations, Marketing & Sales; Entrepreneur; Freelancer
about:
I am, in one word - versatile. I invest in expanding my range by diversifying my experiences. 

From starting my own businesses, studying abroad, joining startups, to immersing myself in new industries (CPG, Fintech, E-Commerce, Retail, Manufacturing, Consulting to name a few), I add value to organizations by connecting seemingly unrelated disciplines.

I have been recognized with high potential ratings across a spread of disciplines from Consulting, Product R&D, Packaging Management, Supply Chain Strategy, Operations, Sales, Analytics, and Marketing.

I bring to the table an analytics translator skill set, an eye for distilling complicated concepts into functional frameworks, and a passion for innovation. I love understanding and developing people and am a strong believer in maximizing an individual's potential. I get involved in recruiting and retention missions to build the most critical resource of an organization - it's talent. 

In my free time, I am a hobbyist photographer, home cook, blogger, artist, and freelancer. These are extensions of my creative passions as I freely experiment with storytelling in different styles.

I love teaching others and am open to speaking, writing, or lecturing opportunities!

about:
Vikas Taneja is a Managing Director & Senior Partner with the Boston Consulting Group.  He is the Global Leader for BCG's Partnerships & Alliances. Vikas also is on the Global Leadership Team of BCG's Technology, Media, and Telecom practice and helped launch BCG's GrowthTech business.  Vikas previously was the leader of BCG's Marketing and Sales practices in the Americas and the Global Head of the Sales and Go-to-market topic for BCG. Vikas also manages BCG's relationship with B Capital and is a Founding Advisor to B Capital. 

Mr. Taneja’s commercial focus has been on achieving profitable growth at major corporations.  He has led major programs to improve business performance through improving sales productivity, product portfolio improvements, process reengineering, and organization restructuring.  In particular, Vikas has worked extensively with software, technology, and IT services companies on topics such as improving software sales process and compressing turnaround times, sales growth, sales productivity, and metrics. 
 
Prior  to joining BCG, Vikas worked at ARCH Technology Partners where he evaluated and helped commercialize new technologies emerging from University of Chicago’s academic labs and medical school.  Vikas has also worked in the Information & Technology group at McKinsey & Co. 

Vikas received his MBA with Honors in Economics & Finance from the University of Chicago.  He also holds a Bachelor of Arts and Sciences in Computer Systems Engineering and Economic Development from Stanford University.    

Mr. Taneja previously led the Boston chapter of Pratham, an India-based organization that has worked with over 4 million children to help them achieve literacy and basic mathematics skills.
